intro:
Use it to set a number where the feel of the change matters more than the exact figure: a brush size, an opacity, a zoom. The value updates while the hand moves, so whatever it drives can follow live.

The default `fill` slider writes its name at the start of the track and its value at the end, so a panel of settings is a column of bars rather than labels, tracks and numbers to line up. Give every slider a `label`; it is also what a screen reader announces.

For a number that has to be typed exactly, such as a price or a page count, use an [Input](/docs/web/components/input). For a choice between a few named options, use [Tabs](/docs/web/components/tabs) or a [Select](/docs/web/components/select).
usage:
<Slider label="Opacity" defaultValue={80} format={{ style: "unit", unit: "percent" }} />

<Slider variant="line" label="Zoom" min={25} max={400} defaultValue={100}>
  <Slider.Step by={-25} aria-label="Zoom out">
    <MinusIcon />
  </Slider.Step>
  <Slider.Step by={25} aria-label="Zoom in">
    <PlusIcon />
  </Slider.Step>
</Slider>

parts.Step: A button beside the track that moves the value by `by`. One with a negative `by` stands before the track and one with a positive `by` after it, wherever they are written. It is disabled at the end it moves towards, and does nothing on a range.

examples.title: Line
examples.description: `variant="line"` is a thin track with a round knob, for a toolbar or a player where the value is shown elsewhere or not at all. Here two `Slider.Step` buttons zoom out and in by 25%, and the number beside it reads the held `value`.

examples.title: From the centre
examples.description: `origin="center"` fills from the middle of the range towards the value, for a value that can go either way from nothing. A hairline marks the middle. Pass a `format` function to write the sign.

examples.title: A range
examples.description: A `value` or `defaultValue` of two numbers draws two handles and fills between them. The value reads as both ends, each written by `format`. Here the part of a clip to keep, and the hours a studio is open.

examples.title: Steps
examples.description: With 12 steps or fewer, a notch on the top and bottom edges marks every step, so it is clear the value moves in jumps. The text runs between the notches and never crosses one. `ticks` turns them on or off by hand. A `format` function can name each step instead of numbering it.

examples.title: Colours
examples.description: `color` sets the fill and the handle. Keep `neutral` for a panel of settings, where a column of coloured bars would compete with the work beside it. Use a colour where the value carries a meaning, such as warmth or a level that becomes risky.

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: `sm`, `md` and `lg` set the height of a `fill` slider and the size of its text. `md` matches the height of a small button.

notes:
### Pointer and keyboard

A press away from the handle glides the fill there; a drag follows the pointer with no easing. Pulled past either end, the track stretches a few pixels and springs back on release.

The arrow keys move by `step` and Page Up and Page Down by `largeStep`, 10 steps by default. Home and End go to `min` and `max`.

### Writing the value

`format` takes number-format options, such as `{ style: "unit", unit: "percent" }`, or a function from the number to a string. Either way it also writes what a screen reader reads, so a value written as `1.40×` is read as that rather than as 1.4.

### Forms

Give it a `name` and it submits its value with the form it is in. A range submits both numbers.

With reduced motion turned on, the fill moves without gliding and the track does not stretch.
